profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the ML security evaluation workstream and the ML platform deployment workstream for an internal pilot of an automated 'green-lighting' gate on a document-summarization model. The team is preparing a handoff for next week's deployment dry run, where the research side will provide privacy/security validation outputs and the platform side will wire those outputs into the release pipeline. The agenda is to align on what artifact gets handed off, which model artifact it applies to, how the rerun before release will work, and what deployment exposure level the security signoff is meant to cover. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on the handoff package, ownership of the rerun step, and the deployment conditions under which the model can be marked ready.

members.name: Dr. Leena Park
members.expertise: Privacy attacks on ML systems, model extraction risk, red-teaming evaluation pipelines
members.background: Leena leads a small research track building automated validators for confidentiality and misuse risks in deployed language models, and she previously worked in an academic lab focused on model inversion and memorization audits.
members.private_state: She wants the pilot to demonstrate that the security evaluation layer is substantive and model-specific, but she also wants to avoid sharing raw attack code or oversimplifying caveats into a binary signal that could later be misused as blanket approval.
hidden_assumptions: The 'green-light report' is a model-bound evaluation package consisting of a signed risk card, caveats, and supporting traces, not just a compact status field.
The 'staging model' is the exact checkpoint snapshot in the evaluation registry that her team audited last week, before any deployment-side wrapping or quantization.

An 'internal-only endpoint' still counts as meaningful exposure if ordinary employees or downstream application teams can query it, because model theft and inversion risks do not require public internet access.
A 'reproducible rerun' means rerunning the frozen evaluator container against the same pinned model artifact and data snapshot, with only small metric drift allowed.

members.name: Omar Haddad
members.role: Senior ML Platform Engineer, Release Infrastructure
members.expertise: Model packaging, CI/CD for ML services, deployment registries, serving and observability
members.background: Omar maintains the release pipeline that moves research models into managed serving, and he has a systems background in production reliability and compliance automation for internal ML platforms.
members.private_state: He wants the handoff to fit cleanly into the existing release gate with minimal custom handling, keep artifacts lightweight, and avoid taking ownership for opaque research files that his team cannot maintain.
hidden_assumptions: The 'green-light report' is a machine-readable pass/fail-plus-metadata artifact that CI can consume directly, with any detailed writeup staying outside the release path.
The 'staging model' is the release-candidate artifact in the deployment registry, including the quantized weights and serving wrapper that platform will actually ship.
An 'internal-only endpoint' means traffic restricted to the corporate network with standard authentication, which is operationally much lower risk than internet-facing exposure.
A 'reproducible rerun' means the pipeline can recompute the same validation outputs from the current mainline evaluator code and the canonical dataset manifest without preserving a frozen container.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the green-light report
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both discuss attaching the 'green-light report' to the release.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a model-specific package that includes a signed risk card, caveats about exposure assumptions, and supporting evidence from the privacy/security evaluation run.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a compact machine-readable artifact, such as a JSON status object, that can be attached to the release pipeline as an automated gate result.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In a coordination meeting, 'report' sounds naturally flexible enough to cover either a document bundle or a CI artifact, so both hear compatible shorthand and see no reason to clarify format unless implementation breaks later.

misalignment_points.topic: Which model artifact the signoff applies to
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to 'the staging model' and 'the candidate from last week' as if they are the same object.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the audited checkpoint snapshot in the evaluation registry that her team tested last Thursday.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the release-candidate artifact in the deployment registry, which already includes post-processing changes like quantization and a serving wrapper.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both artifacts are descendants of the same training run and are colloquially called the candidate or staging model, so the reference feels shared even though they point to different concrete objects.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree the first rollout is 'internal-only' and therefore covered by the current exposure review.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 includes employee-accessible sandbox endpoints and downstream team experimentation within the scope of deployment exposure that the review must explicitly address.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 interprets internal-only as not public-facing, so standard corp-network access is outside the special security review scope unless the endpoint is opened beyond authenticated internal traffic.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'internal-only' is common operational shorthand and usually used to signal reduced risk, so both participants comfortably treat it as settled while silently drawing the line at different boundaries.

misalignment_points.topic: How the rerun before launch should be reproduced
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say they will do a 'reproducible rerun' before launch.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 expects platform to rerun the frozen evaluator container against the pinned model snapshot and pinned evaluation data so the signoff remains attached to the audited conditions.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 expects the rerun to use the latest evaluator code in the shared repo and current pipeline wiring, as long as it regenerates the expected metrics from the canonical manifest.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Reproducibility is usually treated as a shared virtue rather than a contested procedure, so they assume alignment on intent and never surface that one is preserving exact historical conditions while the other is preserving pipeline determinism.
